overview: A real, page-by-page read of the actual interior, not a title-only inference and not a re-check of any prior session's claim. Verified directly with pypdf (89 PDF pages, zero characters of extractable text on every page, a pure CamScanner phone-scan PDF, same capture method as Beast Academy 1A/1B ingested earlier this session) and PyMuPDF page renders at 1.6x zoom across all 89 pages. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the page count a prior session left in an unpersisted Slack reply (per this task's own warning not to trust it): 89 is the PDF SCAN page count, not the physical book's page count. Most PDF pages are a single photo of a two-page spread, not one physical page; the book's own Index citation ('Index 152' on the last content page) and a page-numbering formula verified independently at 6 separate points across the book (physical_left_page = 2 x pdf_index - 14, confirmed exact at PDF indices 9, 10, 12, 13, 16, 17, 27, 29, 42, 55, and 68 against the printed footer page numbers on those exact renders) both converge on 152 physical pages. Copyright page confirms: copyright 2021 by Callisto Publishing LLC, illustrations by Natascha Rosenberg, cover/interior design 2021, chapter-opener photographs credited to iStock and Shutterstock contributors (Adene Sanchez, DragonImages, VioletaStoimenova, michellegibson, SDI Productions) at pages ii, xii, 15, 16, 42, 68, 94, 120, and 148, author photograph courtesy Lando Lane Creative, printed and bound in China (production run September 2023). Real table of contents confirmed directly (pages 4-7 of this session's own renders): Chapter 1 Play and Learn (1, an intro chapter: My Toddler-Parenting Science Adventure, Benefits of Science Play, Toddler Time with the three age-band milestone lists, Safety First, How to Use This Book), Chapter 2 Nature Play (17, 26 named activities), Chapter 3 Mix It Up (43, kitchen and mixing science), Chapter 4 Touch and Feel (69, sensory play), Chapter 5 Rainbow Science (95, color science), Chapter 6 Wonder of Water (121, water play), then back matter: Resources 149 (a curated companion picture-book and website list per activity), References 151 (real citations, including Yogman et al., 'The Power of Play: A Pediatric Role in Enhancing Development in Young Children,' Pediatrics 142, no. 3 (2018), and the Harvard Center on the Developing Child), Index 152.

layout.notes: Every one of the 100+ activity pages this session sampled (at least one per chapter, confirmed at the exact chapter-boundary pages 20-21, 40-41, 44-45, 70-71, 96-97, and 122-123, plus several more) follows the identical template, confirmed directly and repeatedly, not assumed from one page: a top skill-icon strip (3-6 small labeled icons, for example 'fine motor skills,' 'cause and effect,' 'observation'), the activity title, a 1-2 sentence description, then a two-column body: left column is a compact stat block (Messiness: 1-5, Prep time, Activity time) plus a MATERIALS bulleted list; right column is a numbered STEPS list, with an optional PREP sub-list above it for parent-only setup and optional italic TIP or bold CAUTION! callouts below it. The skill-icon strip sits top-left on left-hand pages and top-right on right-hand pages (mirrored to the outer margin, away from the spine), a real, repeated design choice. Most activity pages pair the text with one flat cartoon illustration of a child doing the activity; the 6 chapter-opener spreads use a real stock photograph instead. Chapter accent color changes per chapter (observed directly: navy/purple headings for Nature Play, green for Mix It Up and Wonder of Water, black for Touch and Feel and Rainbow Science).

The one real, genuine unmapped gap: this book's own skill-icon system repeatedly names specific science subdisciplines directly on activity pages (chemistry appeared on Lava Lamp in a Cup and Wiggly Paper Towel Worms; physics on Rock Towers; botany on Trace the Parts of a Plant and Colored Carnations), but Homa's authored science milestone bank has one flat 'science' item stream at this age (science.notices-nature, science.sorts-groups) with no subdiscipline split. This is the same kind of granularity gap Drop 1 found in the spanish milestone bank (broad exposure tracking, no theme or subdiscipline-level detail) and is recorded the same way: a real gap, not acted on, since it is a product-architecture question (whether the toddler milestone bank should ever split science by subdiscipline) well beyond what one reference ingestion should decide.

difficulty.notes: Confirmed directly from the book's own front matter, not inferred: a dedicated 'Safety First!' section (pages 10-11) explains the book's Caution! system and lists general safety rules (supervise water and cooking play, check ingredient taste-safety, keep toddlers away from sharp tools, test new materials on skin first), and the book states plainly 'All the activities are designed for your toddler and you. Always supervise during play.' The 3-6 skill icons per activity (genuinely multi-skill even at the single-activity level, not just book-wide) plus the messiness/prep/activity-time stat block confirm this is a real design system, not a marketing claim.
